problems.what: 'play asleep' and 'obey anyone' changed to 'go asleep' and 'anything you don't want'
problems.replace: a way to make you go asleep, surrender, or do anything you don’t want to do
problems.with: something where you have to surrender, play asleep, or obey anyone

problems.what: 'instead of adding depth' for the already-trancey case
problems.replace: and making sure you are contained
problems.with: and making sure you are contained instead of adding depth

problems.what: the target qualities incl. 'still able to stop', and 'depth is optional'
problems.replace: choose as deep a trance as you need:
problems.with: choose as deep a trance as you need: focused, warm, receptive, embodied, and still able to stop. Depth is optional.

problems.what: 'only when that helps' for deepening
problems.replace: It may also be deepening.
problems.with: It may also be deepening, but only when that helps.

problems.what: the alternatives to counting (conversation, story, movement, repeated sound, curiosity); 'easy' replaces 'one way in'
problems.replace: Counting is easy but you can do all sorts of things to gather up attention.
problems.with: Counting is one way in, but conversation, story, movement, repeated sound, and curiosity can also gather up attention.

problems.what: 'say so' became 'it's OK to tell'; covert-induction point turned into pretending it's elegant
problems.replace: It's OK to tell people when you're doing this rather than pretending it's all very elegant and flowing.
problems.with: Say so when you use them; being elegant doesn't excuse a covert induction.

problems.what: 'if the useful response is already happening, build from it'
problems.replace: to see if it works.
problems.with: to see if it works. If the useful response is already happening, build from it.

problems.what: the condition: switch when the metaphor stops helping
problems.replace: If you do change metaphors do it consciously.
problems.with: Switch consciously when the metaphor stops helping.

problems.what: qualities borrowed 'from other inductions'; warmth and steadiness examples lost
problems.replace: steal qualities from other inductions
problems.with: borrow qualities such as warmth or steadiness

problems.what: 'if that's appropriate to the context' puts a condition on no-response as a signal
problems.replace: , if that's appropriate to the context

problems.what: 'you don't have to find a problem' lost; worthwhile purposes became 'try to use it for something good'
problems.replace: Try to use it for something good (e.g. more love, play, confidence, creativity, communion with life, whatever).
problems.with: More love, play, confidence, creativity, communion, whatever, are all worthwhile purposes, and you don't have to find a problem.

problems.what: the instruction to deal with immediate support instead of exploratory hypnosis
problems.replace: unable to look after yourself.
problems.with: unable to look after yourself - get immediate support instead of exploratory hypnosis.

problems.what: the kinds of encouragement: spacious listening, warm company, firmer invitation to stay with a feeling
problems.replace: encouraging, warm, firm, or whatever
problems.with: spacious listening, warm company, or a firmer invitation to stay with a feeling

problems.what: 'know how to change direction, no need to supervise every moment' became 'skill easier, relax effortlessly'
problems.replace: Once the skill is easier to apply, you can relax into using it effortlessly.
problems.with: Once you know how to change direction, you don’t need to supervise every moment.

problems.what: 'lack of effort produces the maximum benefit' is not in the published text
problems.replace: It is the lack of effort that produces the maximum benefit.
problems.with: Let a useful response become easier and less effortful.

problems.what: 'a no remains no; silence doesn't authorize adding things' turned into 'you don't have to say anything'
problems.replace: Saying no is enough. You don’t have to say anything.
problems.with: A no remains no; silence doesn’t authorize a narrator to add something you haven’t agreed to.

problems.what: 'your subject' invented; published is the response you got versus what the script expected
problems.replace: from what your subject is responding to, not what you intended
problems.with: from the response you got, not the response the script expected

problems.what: examples: a thought, sound, movement or objection may change where the practice goes
problems.replace: whatever happens can be developed.
problems.with: whatever actually happens can be worked with: a thought, sound, movement, or objection may change where the practice goes.

problems.what: 'keep safety and exit instructions plain' became what the subject needs to know
problems.replace: The subject needs to know they are safe and how to leave the experience.
problems.with: Keep safety and exit instructions plain.

problems.what: Appendix B holds the richer language tools, not safety wording; 'after the induction' lost
problems.replace: The language skills that facilitate these are described in Appendix B and used in Let the next response guide you
problems.with: Appendix B teaches the richer language tools, and Let the next response guide you shows how to use them after the induction

problems.what: the opening phrase is chosen by the reader, not 'the opening phrase for that practice'
problems.replace: include the opening phrase for that practice
problems.with: choose an opening phrase

problems.what: 'settle ... somewhere they can rest for a little while'
problems.replace: As your eyes look somewhere in the room,
problems.with: Let your eyes settle somewhere in the room, somewhere they can rest for a little while, and

problems.what: 'letting what is already there come into view' became plain 'seeing what is there'
problems.replace: seeing what is there
problems.with: letting what is already there come into view

problems.what: sentence breaks off at a comma; 'may reach you ... without needing you to arrange either one' lost
problems.replace: And as you notice the anchor, perhaps a sound or the feel of the breath,
problems.with: And while you notice that, a sound may reach you, or a breath may draw your attention, without needing you to arrange either one.

problems.what: 'whatever you can actually feel'
problems.replace: the pressure, the feel of it.
problems.with: the pressure, whatever you can actually feel.
